messages.content: How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?

function.name: calculate_vector_angle
function.description: Calculate the angle of a vector based on its X and Y components. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

X_component.description: The X component of the vector. This is a float type value.

Y_component.description: The Y component of the vector. This is a float type value.

use_degrees.description: If true, the result will be in degrees. If false, the result will be in radians. Default is false.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?" They want to find the angle of the force for a given momentum. Likely they have momentum vector and want to find angle of force? But force is derivative of momentum: F = dp/dt. If momentum is known as a vector, the force direction is the direction of change of momentum. If momentum is constant, force zero. If momentum changes, the force direction is along the change vector. So angle of force relative to something? They might want to compute angle of a vector given its components. We can use arctan2(Y, X). Use degrees or radians. We can call the function calculate_vector_angle. Provide example. Also explain physics: Force is derivative of momentum. If momentum vector is given, you need its time derivative. If momentum is constant, no force. If momentum changes, the force direction is along the change. So angle of force relative to x-axis: arctan2(dP_y/dt, dP_x/dt). If only momentum magnitude and direction known, can't find force angle without time derivative. So answer: need to know change in momentum. Provide formula. Also mention that if momentum vector is given as (p_x, p_y), then angle = arctan2(p_y, p_x). But that's angle of momentum, not force. So clarify. Provide code using function.
